related_questions.question: How quickly after exposure do you test positive for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Generally, it takes 2-14 days after exposure for COVID-19 symptoms to appear, and you may test positive for the virus during this period. For the Omicron variant, the incubation period (the time between exposure and symptom onset) is typically around 3 days. Testing too early, before 5 days after exposure, can result in a false negative.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms can appear anytime between 2 and 14 days after exposure, according to the CDC.

list.title: Testing:
list.snippet: To get the most accurate results, it's best to wait 5 days after exposure before testing.

list.title: Omicron Variant:
list.snippet: The Omicron variant tends to have a shorter incubation period, with symptoms appearing around 3 days after exposure, according to WebMD.

list.title: False Negatives:
list.snippet: If you test too early, you may not have enough virus in your system to be detected, leading to a false negative result.
